subject: Post-demo alignment: SDK bootstrapping, response schema & streaming edgecases
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Patel <amit@edgeplatform.com>, Sophie Li <sophie@edgeplatform.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 14:32:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo alignment: SDK bootstrapping, response schema & streaming edgecases

Thanks again for taking the call earlier — great to see the use case for medium-length conversational search + a lightweight reranker. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical workshop: 

Recap (what we covered)
- POC goals: integrate Redwood inference for chat-based user support search; use embeddings + small reranker to surface high-recall candidates, then structured response for tool-calling to fetch account details.
- Platform choices: Hosted API for quick iteration, Dedicated if you need predictable throughput later.
- SDK bootstrapping: we recommended our JS/Go SDKs for rapid proof-of-concept.

Open technical items we promised to clarify (short):
1) Auth: API key vs mTLS/OAuth options for Private deployment and where to store KMS keys.
2) Routing: how to pin traffic to lower-latency variants and fall back to cheaper quantized models on overload.
3) Response schema: structured output for tool-calls vs freeform chat — how to enforce JSON schema and handle failures.
4) Request/response semantics: chat vs completions tradeoffs, tokenization/ budgeting, max_tokens, stop sequences, and streaming behavior (especially if you rely on stop tokens to end a streamed response).
5) Embeddings + reranker: vector size, batching guidance, and optimizing top_k for recall vs cost.

Attachments: I attached a minimal config example for SDK bootstrapping and a short PDF with our post-demo notes.

Next steps I propose:
- Technical workshop (90 min) with your engineers and our applied ML + infra team next week — propose Tue 5/18 or Wed 5/19.
- Laura to run a short readout on schema enforcement patterns and Marissa to run through embedding/rerank configuration.

If that looks good, I’ll send a calendar invite and a short agenda.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

From: Amit Patel <amit@edgeplatform.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sophie Li <sophie@edgeplatform.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 16:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo alignment: SDK bootstrapping, response schema & streaming edgecases

Karthik — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying questions from our infra/ML side so the workshop can be focused: 

1) Chat vs completions: our search flow currently uses a single-turn completion for summary generation (we call an internal summarizer). If we switch to chat endpoints, do we lose determinism for a single-turn summary, or is it purely an API difference? Any guidance on what to use for single-turn vs multi-turn?

2) Tokenization and max_tokens: we need to budget tokens precisely. Does max_tokens count output tokens only (per Redwood API)? How should we think about tokenization differences across model families (e.g., Llama2 vs open-3b) when predicting costs?

3) Stop sequences & streaming: our frontend relies on the stop sequence to know when to render the final state; with streaming, if a stop sequence triggers mid-stream, do you close the stream immediately or send a terminal token? Are partial tokens possible?

4) Embedding sizing: our vector store uses 1536-length vectors already. Which embed model do you recommend for reranking vs for semantic similarity? Also any best-practices for batching embed requests to reduce latency when we have bursts?

If you can have Laura or Marissa weigh in on the above, that will help us prep for the workshop.

— Amit
Principal Infra Eng, EdgePlatform

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Patel <amit@edgeplatform.com>, Sophie Li <sophie@edgeplatform.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 18:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo alignment: SDK bootstrapping, response schema & streaming edgecases

On Fri, May 14, 2027 at 4:08 PM Amit Patel <amit@edgeplatform.com> wrote:
> 1) Chat vs completions: our search flow currently uses a single-turn completion for summary generation (we call an internal summarizer). If we switch to chat endpoints, do we lose determinism for a single-turn summary, or is it purely an API difference? Any guidance on what to use for single-turn vs multi-turn?

Short answer: API shape vs model prompting.
- Chat endpoints are structured (role/message pairs) which make multi-turn easier to manage (system/user/assistant separation). For single-turn summaries you can absolutely use a chat endpoint and pass a single user message — determinism depends on the prompt/template and temperature, not the chat API itself. If you need reproducible tokens, set temperature=0 and fix max_tokens and stop sequences.

- Completions endpoints (single prompt string) are slightly simpler for legacy stacks but lack explicit role separation. Either can be used; for POC we typically use chat for future-proofing (tool-calls and function/schema support).

> 2) Tokenization and max_tokens: does max_tokens count output tokens only (per Redwood API)? How should we think about tokenization differences across model families when predicting costs?

- In Redwood API: max_tokens refers to output tokens (the decoder). Total token usage billed = tokens_in + tokens_out. tokens_in is the tokenized length of your prompt/messages; tokens_out is what the model generates. So plan for both.
- Tokenizers vary by model family. For cost estimation, run a small tokenization pass (our SDK exposes tokenizer.token_count(prompt, model)) before sending large batches. We also recommend a safety margin (e.g., +10%) when estimating, because different tokenizers handle certain unicode/emoji differently.

> 3) Stop sequences & streaming: with streaming, if a stop sequence triggers mid-stream, do you close the stream immediately or send a terminal token? Are partial tokens possible?

- Behavior: streaming sends incremental chunks of generated text. When the model emits a stop sequence we consider the response complete and the runtime sends a final event marking completion. Practically: you will receive the final chunk that includes the stop sequence (unless you requested that stop tokens be stripped). After that final chunk a terminal "done" event is sent and the stream is closed.
- Partial tokens: streaming is chunked at token boundaries — you won't see half-utf8 bytes or partial token codepoints. However, you may get chunks that split words (token-level splitting) depending on tokenization, so client code should buffer until the final event.

> 4) Embedding sizing: our vector store uses 1536-length vectors already. Which embed model do you recommend for reranking vs for semantic similarity? Any best-practices for batching embed requests?

- Recommendation: for reranking we often use the dense-embed-1536 model (high-quality, matches your vector size) or dense-embed-1024 if latency/cost constrained. For semantic-similarity you can use the same model — tuning top_k and score normalization often yields more gain than changing model.
- Batching: send embeddings in batches sized to match your network/latency sweet spot. We have seen good throughput at batches of 32–128 vectors on hosted API; Dedicated can push larger batches. Also enable async ingestion to your vector DB so you decouple embed latency from query latency.

Implementation tips (quick):
- SDK: use the SDK's request_metadata.headers to include request_id and route hints (region).
- Routing: use our policy tags to pin traffic to low-latency model variants and set a fallback_model that is quantized for cost-based overflow.
- Schema enforcement: use tool-calling with an explicit JSON schema; the runtime validates and returns a structured 'tool_call' object. Implement an out-of-band fallback if validation fails (we provide a best-effort parser + raw_text fallback).

I'll be on the workshop to walk through concrete examples. Attaching a tiny snippet in the config file I shared that shows token_count usage and streaming handler pseudocode.

— Laura
Staff Product Engineer, Redwood Inference
